fields.title: Neuralgia
fields.bodyHtml:
Neuralgia: advanced treatment in Israel

Neuralgia is a condition characterised by sharp, piercing, shooting pain along the affected nerve. Israel uses modern approaches to the diagnosis and treatment of neuralgia that relieve pain and improve patients' quality of life.

Diagnosis of neuralgia:

  1. Medical examination and history
    The doctor assesses the symptoms and the history of the illness and carries out a physical examination.
  2. Neurological examination
    Testing of sensation, muscle strength and reflexes to identify the affected nerve.
  3. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    Used to image the nerves and surrounding tissues and look for the cause of the neuralgia.
  4. Electromyography (EMG) and nerve conduction studies
    Tests that help assess nerve function and identify damage.

Treatments for neuralgia in Israel:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Anti-inflammatory medicines.
    • Anti-epileptic medicines, such as gabapentin or pregabalin, to control neuropathic pain.
    • Antidepressants to reduce the pain.
  2. Physiotherapy:
    • The use of heat or cold to relieve pain.
    • Specific exercises to improve mobility and reduce tension in the affected nerves.
  3. Injection therapy:
    • Nerve blocks using steroids and anaesthetics around the affected nerve for temporary pain relief.
  4. Surgery:
    • Where conservative treatment is ineffective, minimally invasive surgery may be recommended to remove the cause of pressure on the nerve.
  5. Minimally invasive procedures:
    • Microsurgery.
    • Neurostimulation.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • Highly qualified specialists: Israeli doctors have extensive experience in diagnosing and treating various forms of neuralgia.
  • Modern equipment: Israeli medical institutions are equipped with advanced technology, which allows accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach: Every patient is given a personalised treatment plan that takes account of their particular needs and the features of their condition.
  • An integrated approach: Combining different treatments provides a comprehensive approach to managing pain and restoring function.

Treatment of neuralgia in Israel aims to minimise pain and restore patients' normal activity, using a multidisciplinary approach and the latest medical innovations.

fields.title: Orthopaedic oncology
fields.bodyHtml:
Orthopaedic oncology is the field of medicine concerned with diagnosing and treating tumours of the bones and soft tissues. In Israel, patients are offered innovative treatments for cancers of the musculoskeletal system based on the latest scientific research and clinical experience.

Diagnosis in orthopaedic oncology

  1. MRI and CT
    Highly accurate imaging methods that produce detailed pictures of bone and soft tissue, helping establish the size and extent of the tumour.
  2. X-ray
    A traditional but important method of assessing the state of the bones.
  3. Biopsy
    The key method for obtaining an accurate diagnosis, involving the taking of a sample of tumour tissue for histological examination.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  4. PET-CT
    A modern diagnostic method combining positron emission tomography and computed tomography to assess the metabolic activity of tumours and search for metastases in the body.
  5. Laboratory tests
    These include a full blood count, biochemical tests and measurement of specific tumour markers.

Treatment in orthopaedic oncology

  1. Surgery
    The aim of the operation is to remove the tumour while preserving function as far as possible and minimising the loss of healthy tissue. Reconstructive techniques and joint replacement may be used.
  2. Radiotherapy
    Used to destroy remaining cancer cells and reduce the risk of recurrence. It may be given either before or after surgery.
  3. Chemotherapy
    Used to treat certain types of tumour, particularly where metastases are present.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    The newest treatments, aimed at destroying cancer cells with minimal harm to healthy tissue.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach: leading specialists from various fields of medicine work together to develop an individual treatment plan.
  • Advanced technology and treatments: patients have access to the most modern methods of diagnosis and treatment, which improves the chances of successful treatment and of preserving function.
  • Highly qualified specialists: Israel is home to internationally recognised experts in orthopaedic oncology, which guarantees a high standard of medical care.
  • An individual approach to every patient: treatment is planned with every feature of the case in mind, aiming to preserve the patient's quality of life as far as possible.

Orthopaedic oncology in Israel combines highly qualified doctors, innovative treatments and an individualised approach to every patient, delivering the best results in the fight against cancers of the musculoskeletal system.

fields.title: Osteoporosis
fields.bodyHtml:
Osteoporosis: modern treatment in Israel

Osteoporosis is a chronic condition characterised by reduced bone density, which makes the bones more fragile and increases the risk of fractures. The condition often develops unnoticed, without obvious symptoms, and is only discovered after the first fracture.

Diagnosis of osteoporosis

Modern methods of diagnosing osteoporosis in Israel include:

  1. Bone density scan (DXA): The main method of measuring bone density, which allows the degree of osteoporosis to be established precisely.
  2. X-ray: Used to identify fractures and deformities of the bones.
  3. Laboratory tests: Blood tests to measure levels of calcium, phosphorus and vitamin D, and markers of bone metabolism.
  4. CT and MRI: Used for a more detailed study of bone structure and to identify possible complications.

Treatments for osteoporosis

Treatment of osteoporosis in Israel aims to slow the progression of the condition, improve the state of the bone tissue and prevent fractures. The main treatments include:

  1. Drug therapy:
    • Bisphosphonates: Medicines that slow the breakdown of bone tissue.
    • Calcitonin: A hormone that helps regulate calcium levels in the body.
    • Vitamin D and calcium: To strengthen the bones and improve their density.
    • Hormone therapy: Particularly effective for women after the menopause.
    • Antibody treatment (denosumab): A medicine that blocks the breakdown of bone tissue.
  2. Physical therapy and rehabilitation:
    • Exercises to strengthen the bones and muscles.
    • Physical activity programmes to improve balance and coordination, which helps prevent falls.
  3. Dietary therapy:
    • Advice on a diet rich in calcium and vitamin D.
    • Consultations with dietitians to draw up individual eating plans.
  4. Minimally invasive surgical methods:
    • Kyphoplasty and vertebroplasty: Procedures to restore the spine after compression fractures.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  1. A high standard of medicine: Israeli clinics are equipped with modern technology and use advanced methods of diagnosing and treating osteoporosis.
  2. Qualified specialists: Treatment is carried out by experienced doctors specialising in conditions of the skeletal system.
  3. An individual approach: Every patient is given a personalised treatment plan that takes account of their individual circumstances and needs.
  4. A comprehensive approach: Treatment includes not only medicines but also physiotherapy, dietary therapy, rehabilitation and psychological support.
  5. International standards: Israeli medical institutions meet high international standards of quality and safety in treatment.

Treatment of osteoporosis in Israel combines advanced medical technology with highly qualified staff, which ensures that therapeutic and surgical interventions are both effective and safe.

fields.title: Osteosarcoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Effective treatment of osteosarcoma in Israel

Osteosarcoma is an aggressive form of bone cancer that requires a comprehensive and innovative approach to treatment. Advanced methods of diagnosis and therapy are available in Israel, delivering a high level of effectiveness and patient-centred care.

Diagnosis of osteosarcoma:

  1. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the bones:
    These allow the position and nature of the tumour to be established precisely.
  2. Biopsy:
    Taking a tissue sample for laboratory analysis to confirm the diagnosis and establish the genetic characteristics of the tumour.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Laboratory tests:
    Basic blood tests indicating cancer activity.
  4. PET-CT:
    Provides a detailed picture of the metabolic activity of the tumour and of any metastases.

Treatments for osteosarcoma:

  1. Surgery:
    • Radical resection of the tumour: Removal of the tumour together with surrounding healthy tissue to prevent recurrence.
    • Limb-sparing surgery: The possibility of preserving the function of the limb, provided the tumour can be removed completely.
  2. Chemotherapy:
    • Chemotherapy before surgery: Used to shrink the tumour and destroy any metastases.
    • Chemotherapy after surgery: Given to destroy any remaining cancer cells and prevent recurrence.
  3. Radiotherapy:
    • Radiotherapy before surgery: Used to shrink the tumour in preparation for surgical removal.
    • Radiotherapy after surgery: Given to destroy any remaining cancer cells and prevent recurrence.
  4. New treatments:
    • Immunotherapy: The use of the patient's own immune system to fight the cancer cells.
    • Targeted therapy: The use of medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells.
    • Stereotactic radiosurgery: Highly precise irradiation of tumours with minimal effect on healthy tissue.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An integrated approach to treatment: A team of specialists in oncology, surgery and radiotherapy works together to develop individualised treatment plans.
  • The use of advanced technology: Israeli medical centres are equipped with modern devices that allow accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • Multidisciplinary case conferences: Regular meetings of specialists to discuss complex cases and take well-founded treatment decisions.

Treatment of osteosarcoma in Israel is based on advanced methods and scientific progress, which makes it possible to achieve high survival rates and give patients the best possible quality of life.
